correctness.rationale: For k algebraically closed of characteristic two and all n>=4, the source constructs G_(s,i)=P_s e_(s-2)(variables among x0..x(s-1) except xi). Derivative sum relation, recursive identities and F=(xi+x_(n-1))G_(n,i)+G_(n-1,i) prove ideal equality. Explicit same-level/adjacent syzygies and Buchberger chain criterion prove leading monomials for all n. Then initial ideal M_n=V_(n-1)+x_(n-1)^2 M_(n-1), standard monomial splitting and h_4=(1+t)^3 establish the symmetric triangular numerator for every n. Zero-coordinate case split proves support; normal quadratic ab+ac+bc gives generic length 2. New independent SymPy Groebner/monomial-Hilbert checks at n=4..7 confirm basis count C(n,2), degree 2*C(n,3), and coefficients; exhaustive leading-monomial chain divisibility and strictly descending syzygy right sides are also checked at n=4..20. Finite checks corroborate but do not establish universal induction.
residual_risks: Universal Buchberger chain step rests on the divisibility and decreasing-pair argument in RESULT.md rather than a formal proof assistant.
No claims on global primary decomposition or Cohen–Macaulayness are established.

value.rationale: The banana graph hypersurface is a canonical natural graph-polynomial family; its characteristic-two Jacobian ring is nonreduced at generic singular components. This theorem obtains all Hilbert coefficients with a structurally symmetric triangular numerator and universal Groebner basis, substantially finer than already-known support, generic thickness and total degree. Exact graded data are independently useful for modular singular-scheme comparison and intersection defects; not a parameter renaming or arbitrary small-instance exercise.
residual_risks: Broader geometric implications such as depth, primary decomposition and embedded associated primes remain unproved and are not claimed.
